# J.A.R.V.I.S. BR — projeto inicial Android

Projeto inicial para Windows sem Android Studio. Inclui:
- Aplicativo Android nativo com interface escura futurista
- Entrada por texto, reconhecimento de voz em português e respostas faladas (TTS)
- Modo demonstração local
- Backend Node.js preparado para conectar a um provedor de IA
- GitHub Actions para compilar APK de teste sem Android Studio

## Gerar o APK pelo GitHub (Windows, sem Android Studio)

1. Extraia esta pasta.
2. No GitHub, crie um repositório chamado `jarvis-br-android`.
3. Envie todos os arquivos desta pasta para a raiz do repositório (incluindo `.github`).
4. Abra a aba **Actions** do repositório.
5. Se necessário, permita workflows nas configurações.
6. Execute **Build JARVIS BR APK** em **Run workflow**, ou faça um commit na branch `main`.
7. Abra a execução concluída e baixe o artefato **JARVIS-BR-debug-apk**.
8. Extraia o ZIP do artefato e instale `app-debug.apk` no Android. Talvez seja necessário permitir instalação de apps desta origem.

## Como configurar a IA online

O app já funciona em modo demonstração. Para IA real:
1. Hospede `backend/` em um serviço Node.js com HTTPS.
2. Defina as variáveis de ambiente `AI_API_URL`, `AI_API_KEY`, `AI_MODEL` e `PORT` no serviço.
3. No arquivo `app/src/main/java/br/com/jarvisbr/MainActivity.kt`, troque `https://SEU-BACKEND.example.com/chat` pela URL HTTPS real do backend.
4. Envie a alteração ao GitHub para gerar novo APK.

O backend espera uma API compatível com o formato de chat completions (`messages` e `choices[0].message.content`). Ajuste o código se o provedor usar outro formato.

**Segurança:** nunca coloque sua chave de API no app Android, em repositório público ou no APK. Guarde-a somente nas variáveis de ambiente do backend.

## Observações
- Este é um protótipo funcional inicial, não um assistente de sistema completo.
- Reconhecimento de voz depende dos serviços de voz disponíveis no aparelho e pode exigir internet.
- O APK gerado pelo workflow é de depuração; não é um APK de publicação assinado.

# Testing and verification

## Use the preconfigured Linux CLI

Run `scripts/setup-linux-playwright.sh` on an Ubuntu worker to install the pinned
CLI, Chromium, Mesa Vulkan drivers, and a persistent Xvfb display. Let the reusable
workflow run this before publishing SSH access. Use `playwright-cli` from Actions
or a fresh SSH shell; let the wrapper supply DISPLAY and the Linux configuration.
Use `playwright-cli -s=check open <url>`, `eval`, `screenshot`, and `close` without
manual browser flags. Load `.github/templates/linux.md` by default. Select `mac.md` instead when
a `mac` label or `#mac` hashtag is present. Match case insensitively. Recheck the actual screenshot after upgrades.

## Capture the Linux WebGPU triangle

Install Playwright 1.63.0 and its full Chromium browser as below. Install
`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `vulkan-tools`, and `xvfb` on Ubuntu. Serve
`tests/fixtures/webgpu-triangle.html` over localhost HTTP. Run:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-runtime xvfb-run -a node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/webgpu-triangle.html --canvas '#wgpu' \
  --backend swiftshader --require-green-triangle --out /tmp/linux-triangle
```

Require green triangle pixels, a usable device, `scene.webgpu.rendered=true`,
and no page errors. Inspect the image. Treat SwiftShader and Mesa llvmpipe as
CPU rendering, not GPU hardware acceleration. Use the headed Xvfb result on
[run 34908797646](https://github.com/AgentsLoop/PlayGround/actions/runs/34908797646)
as the verified 2026-09-15 reference. Do not accept the headless result from
that run: its initial generic pixel check falsely accepted background pixels.
Retain the fixture's GPU reference. Preserve failed diagnostics when investigating
`A valid external Instance reference no longer exists`. Do not infer a single

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a Free Fire–inspired, browser-playable first-person battle royale game (Three.js) in the current repo, since the repo contained only skeleton Gradle/README files and the user request was simply "Free fire".

## Requirements
- Single terse user message: `"Free fire"`; no other explicit user requirements.
- Non-interactive run: clarification question could not be answered; assistant chose to build a Free Fire-themed Three.js FPS/battle-royale web game.
- Runtime harness serves static `index.html` on port 3002 and auto-clicks a button labeled exactly `Play`/`Start`; screenshots at 1440×900 and 390×844.
- Aim for visually polished, AAA-inspired presentation with harsh visual iteration.

## Decisions
- Ignore the Android skeleton in README (no `app/` module exists); build a static three.js game with vendored Three.js r170 so it works offline.
- Use local vendor deps (`vendor/three`), local fonts (`assets/fonts`), procedural textures/audio, no build step.
- 11 bots + player = 12 operators; shrinking zone; two weapons (rifle/SMG); loot pickups; HUD/minimap; BOOYAH win screen.
- Capture compatibility: added `aria-label="Play"` to `#playBtn`; loading screen is `pointer-events:none`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full game scaffold: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/{main,world,player,enemies,weapons,effects,audio,hud,utils}.js`.
- Vendored Three.js r170 module + needed postprocessing/shaders into `vendor/three/`.
- Implemented terrain/island, water, sky, lighting, props/POIs (Porto, Vila, Farol, Ruínas, Fazenda, Campo), loot, bots, weapons, shooting/reload/ADS, zone shrink, audio, HUD, minimap, landing/pause/result screens.
- Verified 3D landing and gameplay load with Playwright; no page errors after fixing `Enemy._shoot` vector bug.
- Fixed duplicate `thumb` declaration; fixed muzzle flash parenting; fixed enemy facing/walk arms; added shadows projection fix.
- Server is running: `python3 -m http.server 3002` in repo root.

### Active
- Visual polish iteration based on screenshots.
- Investigating persistent white soft circular "dots" covering sky/scene in screenshots, still present after removing particles and hiding all sprites via Playwright.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Identify the white dot overlay: compare `/tmp/ff-check/dots-base.png`, `dots-nograin.png`, `dots-nosprites.png`; dots persisted even with `#grain` removed and all `scene` sprites hidden. Likely something in sky/clouds, CanvasTexture cloud sprite textures, or DOM overlay; inspect remaining candidates (cloud sprites are in `world.js`, generated `cloudTex`; also check `#grain` SVG/rendering and any CSS radial gradients).
2. Check whether dots remain in a screenshot with `world.scene` cleared of clouds/sky or with renderer cleared; binary-search by hiding `sky`, `sunSprite`, cloud sprites, `water`, postprocessing bloom.
3. Re-evaluate visuals after dots fix: grass still appears as sparse dark clumps (planned: lighten/scale thinner or improve terrain detail texture), weapon viewmodel is very dark/large, no obvious shadows (shadow projection fix added but not yet visually confirmed), landing camera moved outside island but still shows little water.
4. Improve overall polish: better hut roofs (attempted gable edit), water visibility/coast composition, enemy close-up, HUD mobile occlusion, weapon hand/optic proportions.
5. Re-run capture at 1440×900 and 390×844; inspect both gameplay and landing; ensure zero page errors; verify pointer lock/Play autostart.
6. Possibly add touch controls/mobile fallback; currently desktop-only input.
7. Git state: all changes uncommitted; no commit/push yet.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/index.html`: landing/HUD/pause/result DOM, import map, Play button, favicon.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/styles.css`: full UI styling, responsive rules, loading/grain overlays.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/main.js`: renderer, composer/bloom, world/player/enemies wiring, zone logic, match flow, landing camera, input/events, debug hook `window.__ff`.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/world.js`: island height, terrain colors/paths, water/sky/lights, vegetation, clouds, POIs/loot/spawns, minimap bitmap, shadow config.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/player.js`: movement, camera, weapons, shooting/raycast, health, pickups, HUD updates.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/enemies.js`: soldier models, AI/LOS/shooting, death, manager, near-spawn points.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/weapons.js`: weapon stats/definitions and viewmodels (`buildWeapon`, `createMuzzleFlash`).
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/effects.js`: particles, tracers, impacts/decals, shells.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio gunshots/footsteps/ambience/music cues.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/hud.js`: HUD DOM updates, compass, minimap draw, killfeed, damage numbers/directions.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/src/utils.js`: math, seeded RNG/noise, canvas textures/radial sprite helper.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/vendor/three/`: vendored Three.js r170 module/addons.
- `/home/runner/work/jarvis-br-android/jarvis-br-android/assets/fonts/`: Barlow Condensed + Rajdhani TTFs.
- `/tmp/ff-check.mjs`: Playwright script (desktop/mobile load, click Play, screenshots, error capture).
- `/tmp/ff-dots.mjs`: dot-isolation script (hide grain/sprites, screenshots, scene inspection).

## Important Context
- Local server URL: `http://localhost:3002/`; Python server still running from repo root.
- Playwright runtime: `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright`, config `linux.json`; scripts use `DISPLAY` from `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/display`.
- Latest run: `node /tmp/ff-check.mjs` → no page errors; gameplay screenshots at `/tmp/ff-check/game-desktop.png`, `game-mobile.png`, landing at `landing-*.png`.
- White dots persisted identically in `/tmp/ff-check/dots-base.png`, `dots-nograin.png`, `dots-nosprites.png`, strongly suggesting a non-scene or cloudy-sprite source; dots are soft, varying sizes, spread across sky and slightly over distant terrain.
- World uses fog `0xa9c4c0` density 0.0029, ACES tone mapping exposure 0.98, bloom strength 0.32.
- Spawn: `playerSpawn = { x: 32, z: 56, yaw: -0.78 }` (facing Vila at ~66,24); near enemy spawns `(58,38)`, `(10,40)`, `(46,18)`.
- Enemy orientation fixed via `targetYaw = Math.atan2(-dx, -dz)`; enemy `_shoot` needed its own `_v1/_v2` vectors (fixed).
- Shadow bug likely fixed by `sun.shadow.camera.updateProjectionMatrix()` after setting frustum; not yet visually confirmed.
- Current known visual issues: sparse/dark grass clumps, oversized/dark weapon viewmodel, flat overexposed sky, weak/no visible shadows, little water in landing shot, hut roof geometry may be mismatched (gable peak 0.78 vs ridge 1.18).
- `window.__ff = { world, player, enemies, zone, state, hud, camera, renderer, startMatch }` available for debugging.
